subject: Proposal: 'Transient Surge' carveout & SKU continuity clause for Exhibit C pricing
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@orchardhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: 'Transient Surge' carveout & SKU continuity clause for Exhibit C pricing

Sam — attaching our current redline for Exhibit C plus the worksheet with the tier math. Two items we want to get aligned on before we finalize: 

1) "Transient surge" discount trigger: the current language in Exhibit C allows a discount band to apply if monthly usage exceeds the threshold in any given month. Orchard is asking for a carveout that prevents short-lived spikes (e.g., one-week campaign bursts) from permanently changing the committed tier. We want to propose a narrow carveout rather than removing the trigger.

2) SKU continuity: the order form references "SKU groups" but doesn't define what happens if a SKU is deprecated or rebatched. Ops wants a continuity clause so usage migration doesn't cause unexpected band drops or disputes.

Quick ask: can your team confirm acceptable definitions for (a) "surge window" (we're proposing 14 consecutive days within a calendar month to qualify) and (b) whether SKU-level substitutions within the same product family should be treated as continuity versus a new SKU?

Attachments: ExhibitC_redline_v3.pdf (redline with our suggested carveout wording), PricingWorksheet_20270401.xlsx (tier math).

Proposed next step: 30-minute call with Ops + Procurement + Legal tomorrow to lock language. I can be flexible after 11:30 PT.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Nina Patel <nina.patel@orchardhealth.com>

Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: 'Transient Surge' carveout & SKU continuity clause for Exhibit C pricing

Karthik — thanks for the note and the files. A few quick points from Orchard legal and procurement after a quick read: 

- We like the idea of preventing one-off campaign spikes from re-anchoring a customer to a higher committed tier. However, 14 days within a month still seems short — our procurement team generally wants to see a minimum of 30 days. Can you explain operational impact if we require 30 days?

- SKU continuity: Procurement is fine with a continuity clause if it is tight — e.g., the replacement SKU must be functionally equivalent and within the same published product family with less than 10% pricing variance. Also request a formal notice process (30 days) for SKU deprecation.

- Please confirm whether the discount true-up in the redline is retrospective for the month of change or forward-looking. Our standard is retrospective true-up.

I'm copying Sam (ops) who will weigh in on implementation. If we can get a proposed compromise strike-throughs on the redline, we can escalate to execs for a final sign-off.

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@orchardhealth.com>, Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@orchardhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: 'Transient Surge' carveout & SKU continuity clause for Exhibit C pricing

Nina — appreciate the quick read and the concerns. From a legal/operations balance perspective Redwood can accept the concept of a longer window. Two proposed compromise points for the redline (I'm pasting the short text here and will add as a snippet to the attachment "ExhibitC_legal_snippet.txt"):

1) Surge window: replace the 14-day draft with a 21-day continuous qualifying window within a single calendar month. Rationale: 21 days captures sustained demand while limiting exposure for both parties. Operationally, this keeps ramp detection simple for billing (we don't need rolling-window infra except for monthly aggregation).

2) SKU continuity: accept continuity where (a) replacement SKU is within the same product family as published on the Redwood SKU catalog at the time of substitution, and (b) list price variance <= 15% for the directly comparable metric. Require a 30-day notice and a 60-day operational transition period for true-up reconciliation. 

3) True-up treatment: Redwood proposes retrospective true-up for consumption (to match Orchard's ask) but limited to a single monthly true-up and with a 90-day lookback cap for accounting adjustments.

If Orchard agrees to 21 days and the 15%/30-day notice/60-day transition for SKUs, we can accept the carveout language in Exhibit C and proceed to final signatures. I'm happy to join a 30-minute call; our availability tomorrow is 10:00–11:30 PT.

Subject: Re: Proposal: 'Transient Surge' carveout & SKU continuity clause for Exhibit C pricing — next steps

Thanks everyone — appreciate the constructive back-and-forth. Quick recap & next steps: 

- Orchard legal: preference for 30 days on the surge window.
- Redwood legal: willing to meet in the middle at 21 days if Orchard accepts SKU continuity at <=15% variance and the 30-day notice / 60-day transition.
- Ops note: Sam, can you confirm that the 60-day transition and single-month retrospective true-up are implementable without adding manual reconciliation effort?

If Ops confirms, I'll calendar a 30-minute sign-off call for Monday 10:00 PT and circulate an updated redline that incorporates Kimberly's snippet. If Orchard insists on 30 days for the surge window, we'll need an internal pricing decision on step-change protections; I'll flag that to my manager if we get stuck.

Marissa
